messages:
elena-sales: Hey team — Acme POC is reporting intermittent 429s during their embeddings-heavy demo this morning. They say overall tenant quota looks fine in the console. Can we triage?
omar-support: Thanks for flagging. Do we have a sample request_id or the exact endpoint they're hitting? embeddings or chat?
elena-sales: embeddings.create primarily, model=rwd-embed-large, request id from last hit: req_0a9f3c2b. Happened ~09:18 PT. Customer says it spikes for ~30s then clears.
kai-eng: Quick hypothesis: could be a per-route cap or per-tenant burst window exhaustion. Can you paste the response headers from one of the 429s? specifically x-rate-limit-* or x-rw-* headers.
elena-sales: Pasted from their client logs: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 22
x-rw-route-cap: 100
content-type: application/json
```
priya-se: That looks like the route-level token window hit. But we need to confirm whether "route-cap" is in tokens or requests for embeddings (we switched units last quarter). Omar, can you pull the tenant's token accounting for the last 5 minutes around that timestamp?
omar-support: On it. Also asking customer for a curl of the failing call and whether they were doing batching client-side.
quota-bot: Tenant quota snapshot: total_tokens_used=12,450 (24h), route_cap=100 requests/min, per_route_tokens_window=1,000 tokens/min, current_window_tokens=1,010 -> over by 10 (auto-shed applied).
mike-sre: Confirming Kai's callout — auto-shed will return 429s until window resets. The difference could be due to client-side token counting vs our tokenizer (they may be sending larger batch sizes than they assume).
priya-se: Short-term mitigation: increase the route soft cap for this tenant to 200 requests/min for the demo and add a temporary exception to avoid auto-shed. I'll need approvals for a temporary bump. Elena, can you confirm the customer's expected QPS and whether they can add client retries with exponential backoff?
elena-sales: They expect ~130 small embedding calls/sec during the demo (each ~64 tokens). They cannot change client for today's run. Can we do a one-off bump?
kai-eng: We can do a temporary route-cap bump + enable request-level smoothing to prevent bursts from tripping the window. Steps I'm going to run: 1) validate request ids for the hits 2) check whether KV prefix caching is kicking in (if they re-request same vectors) 3) apply a 1-hour soft bump to route-cap and monitor.
omar-support: Collected logs for req_0a9f3c2b and neighbors, attaching snippet: ```{"req":"req_0a9f3c2b","route":"embeddings.create","tokens":72,"ts":2332109305,"status":"429","reason":"route_window_exceeded"}```
mike-sre: Also check that their API key wasn't shared across multiple parallel clients — token accounting is per key by default for routes. Shared keys multiply apparent QPS.
elena-sales: Customer just confirmed they spin up 5 parallel worker processes by default. Multiply that by 130 and they hit our route cap. They can lower concurrency but need help fast.
priya-se: OK doing the temporary bump now. Will add guard: if total tenant tokens > 1,500 tokens/min we auto-revoke the bump and notify. Kai, can you add quick dashboard to watch x-rw-route-cap-remaining for this tenant?
kai-eng: On it — dashboard widget + logfilter for request ids. Also adding an alert if 429 rate > 5% for >1m.
quota-bot: Action: applied route soft cap bump to 200 requests/min (expires in 1h) for tenant acme-inc. Notifying billing & security.
elena-sales: Customer retested — 429s stopped within 90s. They appreciate the quick help.
mike-sre: Follow-ups: 1) add a note to the account about parallel worker pattern, 2) schedule a post-mortem with SE to discuss token-metering and demo best practices, 3) consider adding per-key concurrency limits to prevent accidental oversubscribe.
omar-support: I'll open a support ticket with the logs and the change history. Assigning to priyase for follow-up.
priya-se: Thanks — I'll prepare a one-pager for the customer on how tokens are counted for embeddings, recommended batch sizes, and suggested retry/backoff patterns.
elena-sales: Perfect — closing the swarm. :tada: Thanks everyone!
